Osiris is the god of the afterlife, the underworld, and the dead in ancient Egyptian religion. He was originally associated with vegetation and agriculture. Set (also known as Seth) is an ancient Egyptian deity representing chaos, violence, deserts, storms, and foreign lands. In some versions of Egyptian mythology, Set is considered to be the father of Anubis (with Nephthys), although other traditions name Osiris or Ra as his father.

[4] Nephthys
Nephthys is an ancient Egyptian goddess associated with death, night, and mourning. She is often depicted as a woman with a basket on her head or as a kite (a type of bird). She is the sister and consort of Set and sometimes Isis. In some myths, she is the mother of Anubis by either Osiris or Set.

[5] Ancient Egyptian religion
Ancient Egyptian religion was a polytheistic system that persisted for more than 3000 years. It involved many deities who were believed to control various aspects of nature and human life. The religion included beliefs about death and an afterlife where souls would be judged by Osiris and guided by Anubis.
